triageSummary: All Semgrep results (59) are INFO-level gas/style optimizations -> discarded. Aderyn yielded 0 high/medium; its 13 low issue types are centralization (owner-trust KI), gas (cache/costly-loop), and style (pragma, PUSH0, custom-error, modifier-once, missing event, missing-zero-check) -> all map to known-issue classes or the noise filter except modifier-ordering, kept as QA. Slither's only non-informational, in-scope detector is one divide-before-multiply (Medium) plus the calls-inside-loop family (Low). 4 Slither low-level-calls are in lib/openzeppelin Address.sol (out of scope). Net: 3 normalized findings, of which 2 are plausibly real (1 precision, 1 unbounded-loop DoS) and 1 is QA-only.

findings.description: _denormalizeAmount(uint256,address) performs a multiplication on the result of a division: scaled = scaled * 1e18 / exchangeRate (L629) divides, then for tokens with decimals > 18 scaled = scaled * (10 ** (decimals - 18)) (L636) multiplies the divided result, losing precision. The <18-decimal branch (L634) is a second division (down-scale to native decimals).
findings.auditorNote: Borderline / likely-low-impact. The true divide-before-multiply ordering only triggers on tokens with >18 decimals AND a non-1:1 exchange rate -- exotic for the stablecoin set this contract targets (USDC/USDT=6, DAI=18). On the dominant decimals<=18 path it is plain down-scale rounding (dust loss in protocol's favor), and the 1:1-rate assumption is a documented known issue. Keep for code-scanner to confirm whether denormalized payout rounding can be gamed; not an obvious High/Medium on its own.

findings.description: External calls inside loops. _getYieldForStrategy (L552) loops over clients = IYieldStrategy.getAuthorizedClients() and makes two external calls per client (totalBalanceOf @558, principalOf @558-ish). This nested loop (yieldStrategies x clients) is reached from claim() (L443), getTotalYield()/_getNormalizedYieldForStrategy, canClaim() (L700), and calculateClaimAmount() (L653) -- all unbounded by the in-scope contract.
findings.auditorNote: Plausibly real availability/gas-DoS surface. yieldStrategies is owner-bounded (trusted), but the inner clients[] array is supplied by the external yield strategy's getAuthorizedClients(); anyone depositing into a strategy can grow that set, so claim()/canClaim()/calculateClaimAmount()/getTotalYield() can become un-callable past a gas-limit threshold. Tempered by the 'external yield-strategy behavior out of scope' known-issue class, but the unbounded loop in the in-scope function is the locus -- flag for econ/code-scanner to weigh as a griefing/DoS vector. Corroborated by Aderyn (costly-operations-in-loop @247, loop-contains-require/revert @453/653) and Semgrep (array-length-outside-loop, state-variable-read-in-a-loop).

findings.description: claim() declares modifiers as `whenNotPaused nonReentrant` -- nonReentrant is not the first modifier, so whenNotPaused executes before the reentrancy guard is engaged.
findings.rawCheck: nonReentrant is Not the First Modifier
findings.auditorNote: QA / likely false-positive in this context. The preceding modifier (whenNotPaused) only reads the `paused` storage flag and makes no external call or state change, so guard ordering is harmless here. Worth a one-line QA note (defensive ordering: put nonReentrant first) but not a security finding. No exploit path.
